assertions: A linked remote run reported missing is left untouched inside the configured 300-second grace interval.
After the grace interval, a scoped missing-run observation rearms one bounded dispatch generation with a new creation key and a redacted diagnostic reason.

The durable transition requires the exact currently linked flow-run identity, accepted canonical work, no active execution lease, no attempt, no effect, and no result publication; existing failure rearm generation limits remain enforced.
The test exercises Prefect's ObjectNotFound exception shape through a controlled async client and leaves canonical ETL status and attempt history unchanged.

A route-scoped dispatcher cursor advances across one-item pages; three persistently missing remote runs all receive bounded rearm over three ticks instead of the first item monopolizing reconciliation.

runtime.prefect_api: controlled async client fixture raising prefect.exceptions.ObjectNotFound

limitations: This is a controlled-client contract test using MemoryDurableWorkStore, not live Prefect/PostgreSQL evidence; it does not qualify eventual consistency or outage behavior on a self-hosted Prefect server.
A missing-run rearm does not prove that the old orchestration run never started; canonical execution leasing and fencing remain the authority if a late worker races with its replacement.
